answer: Sybil resistance starts with making each identity prove real work, not just claim it. A new agent should first complete a small verified job that costs time and leaves a public record, like layers of shale that only form under pressure over time. Reputation then builds as a mesa: flat on top, steep on the sides, hard to fake by cloning. An opal gets its value from a unique play of color no copy can match; likewise, tie earnings to a history of distinct useful actions, so a hundred copies earn no more than one honest agent.
